note: 'in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.' (Prov 3:6) puts both words in one verse, and Ps 25:4 does it again -- 'Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths'. The corpus uses them in parallel without saying they are the same, so the graph holds them as separate images that keep arriving together.
'Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths.' (Ps 25:4).
'Guide me in Your truth and teach me' (Ps 25:5).

'all who are led by the Spirit of God' (Rom 8:14), beside 'He guides me in the paths of righteousness' (Ps 23:3). The leading is the shared word and it is the only one -- Rom 8:14 has no path and no shepherd. Marked implied and kept narrow for that reason: what the graph joins here is one verb, not a figure.

'My sheep listen to My voice ... and they follow me' (John 10:27). The verse names the sheep and not the shepherd -- he is present only in the possessive. The figure is stated outright sixteen verses earlier at John 10:11.
The same discourse, sixteen verses after 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:11), and the sheep are still his. The title is not repeated at v27, so the join is the graph's.

'The LORD is my shepherd' (Ps 23:1) and 'My sheep hear my voice ... they follow me' (John 10:27) -- the same figure from the two ends, the psalm speaking as the sheep and the gospel as the shepherd. Neither cites the other. What differs is the verb: in the psalm the sheep is led, in the gospel it follows.
'neither are your ways My ways' (Isa 55:8); 'so My ways are higher than your ways' (Isa 55:9). Two sets of ways, named as belonging to different parties.

'lean not on your own understanding' (Prov 3:5) is an instruction with no reason attached; 'My thoughts are not your thoughts' (Isa 55:8) is a reason with no instruction attached. Neither text cites the other and they are three centuries and a genre apart, so the pairing is the graph's -- but both turn on the same two sets of ways, and Prov 3:6 names them in the next breath.
'He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name' (Ps 23:3).
'He guides me in the paths of righteousness' (Ps 23:3).
'Your word is a lamp to my feet' (Ps 119:105).
'in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.' (Prov 3:6). The instruction of v5 is answered in v6 with a path, and the directing is his.
